title: Chevrolet Bel Air Engines by Year (1950–1975)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet Bel Air by year, 1950–1975: Stovebolt sixes, the 265 and 283, the 348 and 409, and the big blocks.
intro: The Bel Air name ran on Chevrolet's US full-size cars from 1950 to 1975. It began as the hardtop of the Styleline De Luxe, became Chevrolet's top series in 1953, and from 1959 sat below the Impala.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: Stovebolt years
intro: Before 1955 every Chevrolet had an inline six: the 216 with a manual transmission and the 235 with the Powerglide automatic, until the 235 became the only engine in 1953.

generations.name: Tri-Five
intro: The Tri-Five Chevrolets introduced the small-block V8. It arrived in 1955 as a 265, gained dual four-barrels in 1956 and grew to 283 cubic inches in 1957, when Ramjet fuel injection made 283 hp.
Every engine below was available in all three series, the 150, 210 and Bel Air, including the Nomad wagon.
The longer, lower 1958 car added the 348 W-series V8 above the 283, and the 409 followed in 1961.
From 1965 the full-size Chevrolet offered big-block V8s alongside the six and the small blocks.
The last US Bel Airs were Chevrolet's lowest-priced full-size series. Ratings are SAE net from 1972, and from 1974 the base engine was a 350 V8; no six was offered.

1951|235|105.says: 1951: 'The hydraulic-lifter 235.5-cid version used in Powerglide-equipped cars ... delivered 105 hp at 3,600 rpm.' (line-wide statement for 1951 Chevrolets; article covers the Bel Air hardtop)

1953|235|108.says: Only config listed: 6-cyl. 235cid/108hp 1bbl. Also Collector Car Market Review profile (VMR): 3-speed/overdrive cars 235.5 ci, 7:1 CR, 108 hp.

1953|235|115.name: Collector Car Market Review (VMR International) - 1953-54 Chevrolet profile
1953|235|115.says: 1953 Powerglide cars: compression raised to 7.5:1, 'which bumped the horsepower up to 115'. Mac's Motor City Garage 'Chevrolet Class of 1953' agrees: Blue Flame 115 hp standard with Powerglide.

1954|235|115.says: 'The 235-cid power plant produced 115 hp in stick shift cars and 125 with the Powerglide.' Hagerty 1954 Bel Air also lists 6-cyl. 235cid/115hp.
